program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s target and completion criterion are broadly appropriate, and the repeated valid traces consistently report the jacket open in both images with no visible closing progress. Do not tune the question to force the reference label: the reference is an aggregate constraint, not atomic evidence, and the images appear to support absent rather than yes. For robustness, make the binding explicitly compare the same jacket’s front/closure in source and edit, and ensure the criterion distinguishes fully closed from any observable movement toward closing; judge progress from changed overlap/closure, not merely pose or the jacket swinging. Keep unknown available when the front is occluded or evidence is insufficient. There are no transport, schema, or dependency failures here; the disagreement is semantic/evidential, not execution-related.
